videos.title: Conan O'Brien's 2011 Dartmouth College Commencement Address
videos.summary: 앞 절반은 다트머스를 놀리는 농담, 뒤 절반은 토크쇼에서 밀려난 뒤 겪은 실망이 오히려 새 출발의 계기가 됐다는 진지한 이야기예요.

words.ex: My grandfather loved to impart wisdom over dinner.
words.exKo: 할아버지는 저녁 식사 때 지혜를 나눠 주시는 걸 좋아하셨다.
words.note: impart는 격식 있는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 share를 더 많이 써요.

cloze.s: Old sailors love to ___ about the sea to anyone who will listen.
A good mentor doesn't just give orders; she tries to ___.

vs.s: Professors are expected to ___ knowledge to their students.
vs.why: impart: 지식·지혜를 전해 주다 / impose: 규칙·부담을 강요하다 / imply: 넌지시 암시하다

words.ex: Speaking three languages gave her a crushing advantage in the job market.
words.exKo: 3개 국어를 하는 게 취업 시장에서 그녀에게 압도적인 우위를 줬다.
words.note: 영상에서는 '대졸자는 빌 게이츠 같은 중퇴자보다 압도적으로 유리하다'는 반어적 농담으로 써요.

cloze.s: With twice the budget, the bigger team had ___ over us.
Being fluent in English gave her ___ in the interview.

vs.s: Their star player gave them a ___ advantage; the game was over by halftime.
vs.why: crushing: 압도적인 / slight: 약간의 / fair: 공정한, 꽤 되는

words.ex: He works late to compensate for the time he lost last week.
words.exKo: 그는 지난주에 날린 시간을 만회하려고 늦게까지 일한다.
words.note: "What are you compensating for?"는 '뭘 감추려고 그렇게 과하게 해?'라는 농담조 질문이에요.

cloze.s: He talks loudly to ___ his lack of confidence.
The airline offered vouchers to ___ the long delay.

vs.s: We hired extra staff to ___ the losses from the slow season.
vs.why: compensate for: 손실·부족을 메우다 / complement: 서로 보완해 완성하다 / compete for: ~을 두고 경쟁하다

words.ex: She went to great lengths to keep the surprise party a secret.
words.exKo: 그녀는 깜짝 파티를 비밀로 하려고 갖은 애를 썼다.

cloze.s: Some fans ___ to get tickets, even camping outside overnight.
She ___ to hide the gift, but her son still found it.

vs.s: He ___ to keep his promise, flying across the country overnight.
vs.why: go to great lengths: 갖은 애를 쓰다 / go a long way: 크게 도움이 되다 / go too far: 도를 넘다

words.ex: Growing up with a genius brother gave him a bit of an inferiority complex.
words.exKo: 천재 형과 함께 자라면서 그는 약간의 열등감이 생겼다.

cloze.s: Always comparing himself to his brother gave him an ___.
Her ___ made her doubt every compliment she got.

vs.s: He brags so much that people think he's hiding an ___.
vs.why: inferiority complex: 열등감 / superiority complex: 우월감, 남을 깔보는 태도 / guilt complex: 죄책감 콤플렉스

words.ex: Getting rejected still stings, even years later.
words.exKo: 거절당한 일은 몇 년이 지나도 여전히 쓰리다.
words.note: 영상에서는 disappointment stings(실망은 쓰라리다)로 나와요.

cloze.s: The criticism still ___, even though I knew it was fair.
Losing in the final minute really ___.

vs.s: His harsh comment really ___; I couldn't stop thinking about it.
vs.why: sting: 마음을 쓰리게 하다 / stun: 깜짝 놀라게 하다 / stain: 얼룩지게 하다

words.ex: After the breakup, he went completely off the grid for a month.
words.exKo: 이별 후 그는 한 달 동안 연락을 완전히 끊고 지냈다.
words.note: 원래는 전력망(grid)에 연결되지 않은 생활을 뜻해요. 코난은 이 비유를 일부러 엉망으로 늘려서 웃겨요.

cloze.s: We spent a week ___ in the mountains, with no phone and no internet.
After the scandal, the CEO went completely ___.

vs.s: I'm going ___ this weekend, so don't expect any replies.
vs.why: off the grid: 연락을 끊고 / off the record: 비공개로 / off the hook: 곤경·책임에서 벗어난

words.ex: I had my worst fear realized when my laptop died the night before the deadline.
words.exKo: 마감 전날 노트북이 꺼지면서 가장 두려워하던 일이 현실이 됐다.
words.note: 코난은 이게 오히려 가장 해방감 있는(liberating) 경험이라고 말해요.

cloze.s: When the client walked out, I ___, and somehow I survived.
Nobody wants to ___ on the first day of a new job.

vs.s: When the bank called, my worst fear was ___.
vs.why: realize: (두려움·꿈이) 현실이 되다 / recognize: 알아보다 / relieve: 덜어 주다

words.ex: Young players often emulate the style of their favorite athletes.
words.exKo: 어린 선수들은 좋아하는 선수의 스타일을 따라 하곤 한다.

cloze.s: Young engineers often try to ___ the founders they admire.
She ___ her mentor's calm way of handling clients.

vs.s: He doesn't just copy his hero's jokes; he tries to ___ his work ethic.
vs.why: emulate: 존경해서 본받고 따라잡으려 하다 / imitate: 겉모습·방식을 흉내 내다 / mimic: 우스꽝스럽게 흉내 내다

words.ex: Losing his job became a catalyst for starting his own business.
words.exKo: 실직이 그가 창업하는 계기가 됐다.
words.note: 영상에서는 a catalyst for profound reinvention(완전히 새로 거듭나는 계기)으로 나와요.

cloze.s: The failed launch became ___ big changes in the team.
Moving abroad was ___ my career change.

vs.s: Her speech was a ___ for change across the whole company.
vs.why: catalyst: 촉매, 계기 / catalog: 목록 / casualty: 사상자, 피해자

videos.title: Jim Carrey at MIU: Commencement Address at the 2014 Graduation
videos.summary: 두려움 대신 사랑을 선택하라는 짐 캐리의 졸업 축사예요. 안정적인 직장을 택했다가 해고된 아버지 이야기와 자아에 대한 성찰이 코미디와 섞여 있어요.

words.ex: He scored one goal and milked it for the rest of the season.
words.exKo: 그는 골 하나 넣고 시즌 내내 그걸 우려먹었다.
words.note: 영상에서는 기립박수를 더 길게 우려먹으려 했다는 농담이에요.

cloze.s: He got one compliment from the boss and ___ for a week.
The audience kept laughing, so the comedian paused and ___.

vs.s: She knew the crowd loved the joke, so she ___ for another minute.
vs.why: milk it: 최대한 우려먹다 / nail it: 완벽히 해내다 / blow it: 망치다

words.ex: We were elated when our team's paper got accepted.
words.exKo: 우리 팀 논문이 채택됐을 때 우리는 뛸 듯이 기뻤다.

cloze.s: We were ___ when the offer letter finally arrived.
She looked ___ after hearing she had passed.

vs.s: He jumped up and down, absolutely ___ about the news.
vs.why: elated: 들뜰 만큼 매우 기쁜 / relieved: 걱정이 풀려 안도한 / content: 잔잔하게 만족한

words.ex: Don't slack off just because the boss is on vacation.
words.exKo: 상사가 휴가 갔다고 농땡이 치지 마.

cloze.s: Don't ___ just because the deadline was pushed back.
He started to ___ after he got the promotion.

vs.s: Students tend to ___ near the end of the semester.
vs.why: slack off: 게으름 피우다 / back off: 물러서다 / show off: 자랑하다

words.ko: 투쟁-도피 반응 (위협 앞에서 몸이 긴장하는 상태)
words.ex: Public speaking still puts me in fight-or-flight mode.
words.exKo: 사람들 앞에서 말하면 나는 아직도 극도로 긴장한다.
words.note: 머릿속 상상과 실제 위험을 구분하지 못하면 평생 이 상태로 산다는 맥락이에요.

cloze.s: A sudden loud noise can trigger your ___.
Before the interview, my ___ kicked in and my hands were shaking.

vs.s: When the alarm went off, his ___ took over.
vs.why: fight-or-flight response: 위협 앞 긴장 반응 / learning curve: 익숙해지는 과정 / comfort zone: 안전지대

words.ex: Small startups are often in the vanguard of new technology.
words.exKo: 작은 스타트업이 신기술의 선두에 서는 경우가 많다.

cloze.s: These startups are in ___ of clean energy research.
Young artists were at ___ of the movement.

vs.s: The lab is in the ___ of battery research.
vs.why: vanguard: 선두 / rearguard: 후위, 맨 뒤에서 막는 쪽 / guardrail: 난간

words.ex: A lot of procrastination is just fear disguised as perfectionism.
words.exKo: 미루는 습관의 상당수는 완벽주의로 위장한 두려움일 뿐이다.
words.note: 영상의 핵심 표현: fear disguised as practicality(현실적인 척하는 두려움).

cloze.s: A lot of laziness is really fear ___ caution.
The scam email was ___ a message from the bank.

vs.s: His criticism was really jealousy ___ advice.
vs.why: disguised as: ~로 위장한 / replaced by: ~로 대체된 / regarded as: ~로 여겨지는

words.ex: The company took a chance on a fresh graduate, and it paid off.
words.exKo: 그 회사는 신입 졸업생에게 기회를 걸었고, 결과가 좋았다.

cloze.s: No one would hire him until a small firm decided to ___ him.
I ___ a new restaurant, and it was amazing.

vs.s: Thanks for ___ me; I won't let you down.
vs.why: take a chance on: 기회를 걸어 주다 / take advantage of: 이용하다 / take a toll on: 큰 타격을 주다

words.ex: The small team defied everyone's expectations and won the contest.
words.exKo: 작은 팀이 모두의 예상을 깨고 대회에서 우승했다.

cloze.s: The rookie ___ and finished in the top three.
Sometimes you have to ___ to find out who you really are.

vs.s: The tiny startup ___ everyone's expectations and beat the giants.
vs.why: defy: 거스르다, 깨다 / deny: 부인하다 / defer: 미루다

words.ex: Her first mentor left an indelible mark on her career.
words.exKo: 첫 멘토는 그녀의 커리어에 지워지지 않는 흔적을 남겼다.

cloze.s: That trip left ___ on how I see the world.
Great teachers leave ___ on their students.

vs.s: The war left an ___ mark on the city.
vs.why: indelible: 지워지지 않는 / invisible: 보이지 않는 / inedible: 먹을 수 없는

words.ex: I missed my cue to speak, and the meeting moved on.
words.exKo: 말할 타이밍을 놓쳤고, 회의는 다음 안건으로 넘어갔다.
words.note: 원래 연극에서 배우가 등장 신호(cue)를 놓치는 걸 말해요.

cloze.s: I was daydreaming and ___ to start the slides.
Don't ___; the host will nod when it's your turn.

vs.s: The actor ___ and walked on stage ten seconds late.
vs.why: miss one's cue: 신호·타이밍을 놓치다 / miss the point: 요점을 못 짚다 / miss the boat: 기회를 놓치다

videos.title: The time I hit rock bottom | Ryan Erwin Stand-Up Comedy
videos.summary: 계산대, 영화관, 패스트푸드 아르바이트를 전전한 이야기로 '인생의 바닥'을 웃기게 풀어낸 스탠드업이에요.

words.ex: Thanks to her quick thinking, nobody got hurt.
words.exKo: 그녀의 순발력 덕분에 아무도 다치지 않았다.

cloze.s: Her ___ saved the presentation when the projector died.
It took some ___ to calm the angry customer down.

vs.s: Thanks to his ___, the fire was put out in seconds.
vs.why: quick thinking: 순발력 / wishful thinking: 근거 없는 희망 사항 / overthinking: 생각 과다

words.ex: She re-entered the workforce after five years at home.
words.exKo: 그녀는 5년간 집에 있다가 다시 일터로 돌아갔다.

cloze.s: More students are entering ___ straight after high school.
Half of ___ in this town works at the factory.

vs.s: AI is changing the skills the ___ needs.
vs.why: workforce: 노동 인력 / workload: 업무량 / workshop: 작업장, 연수회

words.ex: When I hit rock bottom, my friends were the ones who pulled me up.
words.exKo: 내가 바닥을 쳤을 때 날 끌어올려 준 건 친구들이었다.

cloze.s: After losing his job and his apartment, he finally ___.
Sometimes you have to ___ before things get better.

vs.s: Sales ___ in March, then slowly started to recover.
vs.why: hit rock bottom: 바닥을 치다 / hit the roof: 몹시 화내다 / hit the road: 길을 떠나다

words.ex: Cheating on the exam would bring shame to the whole team.
words.exKo: 시험 부정행위는 팀 전체에 먹칠을 하는 일이다.

cloze.s: Cheating would ___ the whole family.
The scandal ___ the university.

vs.s: His rude behavior at the ceremony ___ the team.
vs.why: bring shame to: 망신을 주다 / bring peace to: 평화를 가져오다 / bring luck to: 행운을 가져오다

words.ex: You absolutely slayed that presentation.
words.exKo: 너 그 발표 완전 찢었어.
words.note: 원래 뜻은 '죽이다'예요. 영상에서는 이 두 뜻으로 말장난을 해요.

cloze.s: You totally ___ that interview!
She walked on stage and absolutely ___ it.

vs.s: Your presentation was perfect; you ___!
vs.why: slay it: 완벽히 해내다, 찢다 / blow it: 망치다 / fake it: 된 척하다

words.ex: It's a temporary fix, with 'temporary' being the operative word.
words.exKo: 이건 임시 해결책이야. 방점은 '임시'에 있어.

cloze.s: It's a free trial, with 'trial' being ___.
We'll finish 'soon', and soon is ___ here.

vs.s: The plan is 'almost' done, with 'almost' being the ___ word.
vs.why: operative word: 핵심어 / operating: 작동 중인 / optional: 선택적인

videos.title: Success is not a comfortable procedure - Steve Harvey
videos.summary: 편안한 곳에 머물면 거기서 실패한다, 불편함에 익숙해지라는 스티브 하비의 18초짜리 한마디예요.

words.ex: Moving abroad pushed me out of my comfort zone.
words.exKo: 해외로 이사한 게 나를 안전지대 밖으로 밀어냈다.

cloze.s: Public speaking pushes most people out of their ___.
Traveling alone is the fastest way out of your ___.

vs.s: Growth starts at the edge of your ___.
vs.why: comfort zone: 안전지대 / time zone: 시간대 / danger zone: 위험 구역

words.ex: Applying for a visa is a long procedure.
words.exKo: 비자 신청은 긴 절차다.
words.note: 보통 의료·행정 절차에 쓰는 딱딱한 말이라, '성공은 편안한 절차가 아니다'가 더 인상적으로 들려요.

cloze.s: Changing your major involves a long ___ with lots of forms.
The doctor explained the ___ before the surgery.

vs.s: Please follow the safety ___ before entering the lab.
vs.why: procedure: 정해진 절차(단계·규칙) / process: 일이 진행되는 과정 전반 / proceeding: 법적 소송 절차, 회의록

words.ex: If you want to grow, you have to get comfortable being uncomfortable.
words.exKo: 성장하고 싶다면 불편함에 익숙해져야 한다.

cloze.s: If you want to grow, you have to ___.
My coach's best advice was simple: ___.

videos.title: More kindness, less embarrassment. #TedLasso
videos.summary: 창피함이 우리를 작게 만든다는 테드 래소의 장면이에요. 봉오리로 웅크린 채 있는 게 피어나는 것보다 더 아파지는 순간에 관한 이야기예요.

words.ex: Fear of judgment can keep you small.
words.exKo: 남의 평가에 대한 두려움은 사람을 위축시킨다.

cloze.s: Don't let other people's opinions ___.
Playing it safe forever will only ___.

words.ex: She finally busted out of her shell in college.
words.exKo: 그녀는 대학에서 드디어 껍데기를 깨고 나왔다.

cloze.s: She finally ___ her shell in college.
It's time to ___ this boring routine.

vs.s: It's time to ___ your old habits and try something new.
vs.why: bust out of: 박차고 나오다 / burst into: 갑자기 ~하기 시작하다(burst into tears) / break down: 고장 나다, 무너지다

words.ko: 꽃봉오리 상태로 머무르다 → 자신을 드러내지 못하고 웅크리다
words.ex: For years he remained tight in a bud, too afraid to share his ideas.
words.exKo: 그는 생각을 말하기가 두려워 수년간 웅크리고만 있었다.
words.note: 흔히 작가 아나이스 닌의 말로 알려진 문장에서 나온 표현이에요.

cloze.s: Out of fear, he chose to ___ instead of sharing his ideas.

words.ex: She really blossomed after joining the debate club.
words.exKo: 토론 동아리에 들어간 뒤 그녀는 정말 피어났다.

cloze.s: She really ___ after joining the band.
Their friendship slowly ___ into something more.

vs.s: The shy freshman ___ into a confident leader.
vs.why: blossom: 피어나다, 성장하다 / blow up: 폭발하다, 화내다 / break out: 발생하다, 탈출하다

words.ex: I'd rather fail trying than never try at all.
words.exKo: 아예 안 해보느니 시도하다 실패하는 게 낫다.

cloze.s: ___ walk than wait an hour for the bus.
___ ask now than make a mistake later.

vs.s: I'd ___ stay home tonight; I'm exhausted.
vs.why: I'd rather + 동사원형: 차라리 ~하겠다 / I'd better + 동사원형: ~하는 게 좋겠다(경고) / I'd prefer는 to가 필요해요 (I'd prefer to stay)

videos.title: My wife's logic makes me question reality | Andy Woodhull Stand-Up Comedy
videos.summary: 넷플릭스를 같이 보기로 해 놓고 30분째 샤워하는 아내가 '샤워가 아니라 헹구는 중'이라고 우기는 이야기예요. 말싸움에서 늘 지는 남편의 하소연이에요.

words.ex: I'll just rinse off after the gym and meet you there.
words.exKo: 운동 끝나고 가볍게 씻고 거기서 만날게.

cloze.s: Can you ___ the vegetables before cooking?
He jumped in the lake to ___ the mud.

vs.s: I'm not taking a shower, I'm just ___ off.
vs.why: rinse off: 물로 헹구다 / wash off, clean off도 쓰지만 이 장면의 말장난은 rinse off예요

words.note: 샤워(take a shower)보다 짧고 가볍게 물만 끼얹는 느낌이에요. 그래서 아내가 '샤워가 아니다'라고 우기는 거예요.

words.ex: When the critics attacked her plan, she fought back with data.
words.exKo: 비판이 쏟아지자 그녀는 데이터로 반격했다.

cloze.s: I didn't know how to ___ against her logic.
The team ___ and won in the last minute.

vs.s: He was attacked online, but he chose not to fight ___.
vs.why: fight back: 반격하다 / fight off: 물리치다 / fight up은 쓰지 않아요

words.ko: 잠깐 눈을 붙이다 (자는 게 아니라고 우길 때)
words.ex: I wasn't sleeping in class, I was just resting my eyes.
words.exKo: 수업 시간에 잔 거 아니야, 잠깐 눈 감고 있었던 거야.

cloze.s: Grandpa says he's not asleep, he's just ___.
I'm going to ___ for ten minutes.

vs.s: "I'm not asleep. I'm resting my ___."
vs.why: rest one's eyes: 잠깐 눈을 붙이다

words.note: 졸다가 들켰을 때 쓰는 단골 변명이에요. 미국 가족 코미디에 자주 나와요.

words.ex: Open the windows to air out the room after cooking.
words.exKo: 요리하고 나면 창문을 열어 방을 환기해.

cloze.s: We left the tent open to ___.

cloze.s: It's moments of ___ and discomfort that teach us the most.

cloze.s: You can ___ any fear with action.

words.ex: The hike was long, but the view was worth it.

cloze.s: Change isn't easy, but it is always ___.

words.ex: You're capable of much more than you think.

vs.why: capable of + 명사/동명사 / able to + 동사원형

videos.title: Two words that will unlock your confidence | Mel Robbins #Shorts
videos.summary: 남이 날 어떻게 생각할지는 통제할 수 없으니 '그러라고 해(let them)' 두고, 내가 통제할 수 있는 내 행동에 집중하라는 이야기예요.

vs.why: focus on: ~에 집중하다

cloze.s: Trying to control others is just making you ___.

vs.s: Social media can make teenagers feel ___.
vs.why: insecure: 자신 없는 / unsafe: 위험한 / uncertain: 불확실한

words.ex: I'm proud of you for not giving up.
words.exKo: 포기하지 않은 네가 자랑스러워.

cloze.s: Do something every day that makes you ___ yourself.

vs.s: My parents are proud ___ me.
vs.why: proud of: ~을 자랑스러워하는

videos.title: Stop Waiting To Feel Better | Mel Robbins #shorts
videos.summary: 기분이 나아지길 기다렸다가 움직이는 게 아니라, 슬프고 불안한 채로라도 움직여야 나아진다는 이야기예요.

words.ex: After months of work, the project is finally coming together.

cloze.s: Trust that things are about to ___.

vs.s: The plan is finally coming ___.

words.expr: wait for the storm to pass

cloze.s: You're ___ before you step outside.
a: waiting for the storm to pass

a: wait for the storm to pass

vs.s: We decided to wait for the storm to ___.

videos.title: Celebrate the ones who DO, not the ones who WIN | Simon Sinek

words.ex: My family came to cheer me on at the marathon.

cloze.s: We're the ones standing under the lamppost, ___.

words.ex: Everything can change in an instant.

videos.title: Be the Idiot | Simon Sinek

videos.title: Sometimes, You Don't Have to Prove Yourself

words.ex: Thanks for giving me a shot at this role.
words.exKo: 이 역할에 기회를 주셔서 감사합니다.

cloze.s: When someone ___ you a shot, you don't have to prove yourself.

vs.s: The coach decided to give the rookie a ___.

words.ex: My professor opened a lot of doors for me.
words.exKo: 교수님이 내게 많은 기회를 열어 주셨다.

words.ex: If you want to leave early, I'm fine with that.

videos.title: A 3-Step Guide to Believing in Yourself @TED #ted #shorts

words.note: 원래는 '공간을 차지하다'예요. 이 영상에서는 '주눅 들지 않고 당당히 있다'는 뜻으로 썼어요.

words.ex: I'll finish this project no matter what.
words.exKo: 무슨 일이 있어도 이 프로젝트를 끝낼 거야.

cloze.s: I belonged there ___ anybody thought.

videos.title: An Olympic Champion's Mindset for Overcoming Fear @TED #shorts

cloze.s: You have to fight to ___.

vs.why: move forward: 나아가다 / foreword: 서문
